basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models the application and decision case, not the granted right or permit that results from it.
Keeps criterion assessments, consultations and reasons inside the case while evidence stays in its own master.
Distinguishes a reasoned decision by a competent authority from process completion, payment or a status page.
Ends with an appeal route and follow-on cases rather than with ongoing inspection or enforcement.

may: Check an application revision for completeness against the published criteria.
Request missing information on behalf of the case handler.
Propose a criterion assessment with cited evidence for an official to review.
Notify applicants of status changes already decided by the authority.
mustNot: Issue, refuse or revoke a decision without competent authority.
Treat paid fees, submitted evidence or a decision copy as proof of a current grant.
Copy evidence into the case beyond what the stated purpose needs.
Withhold the reasons or appeal route from an applicant who received a decision.
Apply criteria from a different jurisdiction or version than the case was opened under.
requiresHuman: Issuing any decision that grants, refuses or conditions an authorization.
Adverse findings against an applicant or a third party consulted.
Disclosure of case files to parties outside the case.

considerations: Applicants have a right to reasons, equal treatment and an appeal, which automated steps must preserve.
Permits often affect neighbours, workers and the environment, who need a fair hearing in consultation.
Evidence files hold personal and commercial data that must stay purpose-bound.
affectedParties: Third parties and communities consulted or affected

items: A permit case has a case number, an applicant, a requested authorization class and scope, and a competent authority.
It is confused with the granted permit itself, a licence credential or an inspection record.
Unlawful decisions when competence or criteria are wrong.
Delay or loss of a lawful activity through lost submissions or missed deadlines.
Harm to neighbours or the environment when consultation is skipped.
Single Digital Gateway Regulation procedures and evidence exchange (EU 2018/1724).
W3C Verifiable Credentials for issuing the resulting grant evidence.
BPMN 2.0 for modelling the case process.
